svg.title: Compare Cash Yield, Not Headline Awards
svg.desc: diagram id: diag-04-specialty-collected-yield; chart type: horizontal_bars; title: Compare Cash Yield, Not Headline Awards; subtitle: Illustrative earned fees per referred claim on eligible federal rails.; chapter number: 2; epistemic tag: illustrative_model; assumptions note: Each bar uses an independent ten-referral cohort, including referrals producing zero cash, and a hypothetical 25% retained share. Net recovery pools already exclude initial payer collections, unrecovered administrative/entity fees, and agreed casework costs. These are comparison assumptions, not specialty benchmarks, expected returns, or a weighted bridge to annual scorecard revenue. Operator overhead remains to be deducted.; caption: Normalize collections to all referred claims so rejected claims, losses, and unpaid awards reduce yield. Specialty labels do not establish jurisdiction or eligibility.; stages: label: Emergency physician; value: $150 earned per referral; numeric value: 150.0; detail: A $6,000 net incremental cash pool across ten referrals produces $1,500 operator fees at 25%. Screen emergency service circumstances, payer coverage, and the applicable state or federal payment route before filing.; label: Facility anesthesia; value: $200 earned per referral; numeric value: 200.0; detail: An $8,000 net incremental cash pool across ten referrals produces $2,000 operator fees at 25%. Verify the participating-facility context and applicable ancillary service protections rather than relying on the specialty code alone.; label: Facility radiology; value: $100 earned per referral; numeric value: 100.0; detail: A $4,000 net incremental cash pool across ten referrals produces $1,000 operator fees at 25%. Separate professional and technical components, validate service identifiers, and prevent duplicate recovery across component claims.; label: Facility pathology; value: $80 earned per referral; numeric value: 80.0; detail: A $3,200 net incremental cash pool across ten referrals produces $800 operator fees at 25%. Validate covered facility-linked services and permitted batching criteria; similar specialty labels do not make every claim batchable.; label: Covered air ambulance; value: $600 earned per referral; numeric value: 600.0; detail: A $24,000 net incremental cash pool across ten referrals produces $6,000 operator fees at 25%. Apply the distinct air-ambulance requirements in 45 CFR § 149.520 and 42 U.S.C. § 300gg-112; exclude ground ambulance claims from this federal comparison.

text.title: Compare Cash Yield, Not Headline Awards
text.tspan: Compare Cash Yield, Not Headline Awards

rect.title: label: Emergency physician; value: $150 earned per referral; numeric value: 150.0; detail: A $6,000 net incremental cash pool across ten referrals produces $1,500 operator fees at 25%. Screen emergency service circumstances, payer coverage, and the applicable state or federal payment route before filing.

label: Facility anesthesia; value: $200 earned per referral; numeric value: 200.0; detail: An $8,000 net incremental cash pool across ten referrals produces $2,000 operator fees at 25%. Verify the participating-facility context and applicable ancillary service protections rather than relying on the specialty code alone.

label: Facility radiology; value: $100 earned per referral; numeric value: 100.0; detail: A $4,000 net incremental cash pool across ten referrals produces $1,000 operator fees at 25%. Separate professional and technical components, validate service identifiers, and prevent duplicate recovery across component claims.

label: Facility pathology; value: $80 earned per referral; numeric value: 80.0; detail: A $3,200 net incremental cash pool across ten referrals produces $800 operator fees at 25%. Validate covered facility-linked services and permitted batching criteria; similar specialty labels do not make every claim batchable.

label: Covered air ambulance; value: $600 earned per referral; numeric value: 600.0; detail: A $24,000 net incremental cash pool across ten referrals produces $6,000 operator fees at 25%. Apply the distinct air-ambulance requirements in 45 CFR § 149.520 and 42 U.S.C. § 300gg-112; exclude ground ambulance claims from this federal comparison.

text.title: Assumptions: Each bar uses an independent ten-referral cohort, including referrals producing zero cash, and a hypothetical 25% retained share. Net recovery pools already exclude initial payer collections, unrecovered administrative/entity fees, and agreed casework costs. These are comparison assumptions, not specialty benchmarks, expected returns, or a weighted bridge to annual scorecard revenue. Operator overhead remains to be deducted.
